correctness.rationale: The proof uses valid full-family Apéry and minimal-coin statements, independently establishes monotone greedy weight by an exact denomination identity, computes the high Mersenne-coin digits from all binary bits of m, proves the precise final plateau and its first index, and substitutes the unique maximizing Apéry representative. The independent shortest-residue-path verifier checks 161 finite semigroups over 1,072,169 vertices, three further q=63 cases, and carry identities. The infinite theorem is proved symbolically, with no reliance on extrapolation.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-odd-parameter Frobenius question is explicitly posed in the motivating original literature; only two initial-coefficient branches had been evaluated in the published follow-up. The theorem closes every branch by a uniform digit-sum formula requiring only the Mersenne-coin expansion of h≤n, gives the unique Apéry maximizer, and includes an infinite natural family of q=63-type omissions.
